body:
Layered feature enumeration deduplicates defaults against local entries during request/validator resets. The exclusion set currently stores whole Type/object pairs even though equality uses only Type, creating larger repeated sets on warm layered paths.

This PR uses ExceptBy over local keys with the existing Type equality contract and a null-key guard. Deferred snapshots, deduplication/order, custom defaults, mutation/disposal and the no-default path are preserved.

### Benchmarks

Each operation fully enumerates a real PooledFeatureCollection graph through its feature interface, consumes key/value identities and observes a volatile checksum. Warmup retains Keys wrappers; cold construction is excluded.

Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, server/concurrent GC, four cores: one launch per variant/policy, seven internal windows of 4,096 operations. Timing uses default GC; separate allocation runs use `DOTNET_GCDynamicAdaptationMode=0`. Ratios are PR/baseline, with window-median timing and time-separated single-launch uncertainty. Baseline `9a563e814f` C# matches current main `706ec84ff2`; only Features DLL/PDB changes in the consumer. The clean branch preserves the measured candidate’s production/test blobs (`c6d2496c38`).

B/op means scoped executing-thread allocation, calibrated by exact escaping 48/1,048 B controls and zero observer brackets. Both strict process censuses failed with +336 B batch residuals; process/default-HTTP totals remain unvalidated.

| Case | Baseline ns | PR ns | Time C/B | Baseline B/op | PR B/op | Alloc C/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Empty, no defaults | 11.55 | 12.92 | 1.118 | 96 | 96 | 1.000 |
| 7 local, no defaults | 105.88 | 102.42 | 0.967 | 96 | 96 | 1.000 |
| 1 local / 3 defaults | 209.23 | 198.51 | 0.949 | 800 | 720 | 0.900 |
| 7 / 1 / 3 layers | 582.79 | 521.00 | 0.894 | 1896 | 1624 | 0.857 |
| 7 / 1 / 3, 2 overrides | 544.73 | 508.98 | 0.934 | 1896 | 1624 | 0.857 |
| 16 / 1 / 3 layers | 892.77 | 732.91 | 0.821 | 2736 | 2224 | 0.813 |
| 1 local / 31 defaults | 1277.61 | 1173.97 | 0.919 | 2416 | 1904 | 0.788 |

The Keys wrapper is a 24 B estimate per dictionary, retained across pooled resets; new dictionaries pay again. Static selector startup and empty-local-with-defaults net cost are unmeasured. Actual frozen HTTP defaults differ from the representative mutable graph, so 272 B is not a universal request saving. The unchanged empty path moved +1.37 ns.

Release builds passed; twenty-four new contracts passed on candidate/frozen baseline, plus eleven existing tests, covering equality/nulls, duplicates/order, mutation and disposal.

[Method results and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/da82b30d00b3187bced84dfa649bf4b839ffe9c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/FEATURE-CANDIDATE-RESULT.md), [HTTP results and limits](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/da82b30d00b3187bced84dfa649bf4b839ffe9c1/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/FEATURE-HTTP-RESULT.md).

### HTTP revalidation

Fresh matched controls use the original frozen baseline `9a563e814f`, Release .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, default server/concurrent GC, four logical CPUs assigned to the gateway, 200 requests/s, 64 VUs and a fixed 4 ms source delay. Each fresh gateway gets 60 s warmup and 60 s measured traffic. One unchanged source process spans the balanced schedule: baseline, snapshot, enumeration, iterator, scope, baseline, scope, iterator, enumeration, snapshot, baseline. Only the candidate assembly/PDB differs from the frozen baseline.

All response, identity, request-accounting and CPU-counter checks passed, with zero errors or dropped starts. Every measured group completed 12,001 requests except enumeration run 2, which completed 12,000. CPU uses actual completions. No profiler ran; identical one-second state/process observations remained enabled. Native latency samples were checked against completion counts. Effective DATAS/heap count was not exposed and is not inferred.

| Run | CPU ms/request | CPU C/B, both surrounding controls | p95 ms | p99 ms | p99.9 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline-1 | 0.841673 | - | 10.296 | 12.653 | 19.686 |
| enumeration-1 | 0.823910 | 0.9789–0.9936 | 10.203 | 12.680 | 24.775 |
| baseline-2 | 0.829226 | - | 9.834 | 11.829 | 16.288 |
| enumeration-2 | 0.828339 | 0.9989–1.0253 | 10.114 | 12.293 | 23.399 |
| baseline-3 | 0.807881 | - | 10.050 | 12.369 | 20.243 |

Baseline CPU declined 4.01% across the campaign. Ratios show both surrounding controls without correcting away that drift. Requests and five-second blocks are dependent observations, not independent process launches. Matching-window OS/runtime checks validate the CPU counter; their bounds are not full-phase performance error bars. The comparison does not identify JIT or GC as a cause.

[Matched HTTP results, raw data and reproduction](https://github.com/ChilliCream/graphql-platform/blob/1e75ce82d3ec18dea4b2083272e0e946ab7c0872/performance/fusion-fresh-alloc/SHARED-HTTP-REVALIDATION-RESULT.md).

### Verdict

**Abandoned because overall performance benefit remains unproven.** The earlier +16.90% CPU/+26.3% p99 result did not reproduce: CPU and p95/p99 showed no repeated adverse pattern against the matched controls. However, p99.9 increased to 24.775/23.399 ms versus baseline 19.686/16.288/20.243 ms in both orders. Multiple neighboring slow requests contributed, with temporal clustering. Two candidate launches cannot resolve whether this far-tail signal is caused by the change.

The 80–512 B warm scoped allocation saving is supported, but it is insufficient to accept the unresolved repeated tail signal. The PR is closed for insufficient overall evidence, not for a proven CPU regression. No further benchmark retry was used to seek a favorable result.
